'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Yemeni Civil War (2014–present)|Yemeni Civil War]]
**[[Battle of Marib]]
***The [[Saudi Arabia]]-led coalition says that they have killed 160 [[Houthi movement|Houthi]] [[militant]]s in [[Marib]], [[Yemen]], during 32 [[airstrike]]s in the past 24 hours. The coalition also reports that they killed a total of more than 700 Houthis during the past week. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/10/17/coalition-says-killed-160-yemen-rebels-in-battle-for-marib (Al Jazeera)]
*[[Insurgency in Jammu and Kashmir]]
**Militants open fire on a group of non-resident workers from [[Bihar]] in [[Kulgam]], [[Jammu and Kashmir (union territory)|Jammu and Kashmir]], killing two people and wounding another. [https://www.greaterkashmir.com/kashmir/another-non-local-labourer-shot-at-in-south-kashmirs-kulgam (Greater Kashmir)] [https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/india/terrorists-kill-2-more-non-locals-injure-1-in-jammu-kashmir/articleshow/87091250.cms (''The Times of India'')]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[Floods in India]]
**Twenty-six people are killed and dozens are missing as heavy rains affect the [[Indian state]] of [[Kerala]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-asia-india-58940880 (BBC News)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Brunei]]
****[[Brunei]] reports a record 504 new cases of [[COVID-19]] in the past 24 hours, thereby bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 10,860. [https://borneobulletin.com.bn/brunei-logs-record-high-in-covid-cases-deaths/ (Borneo Bulletin)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Saudi Arabia]]
****[[Saudi Arabia]] eases its COVID-19-related restrictions, lifting mandatory [[social distancing]] requirements as well as a requirement to wear [[Face masks during the COVID-19 pandemic|face mask]]s outdoors. [https://www.arabianbusiness.com/industries-culture-society/469804-saudi-arabia-eases-coronavirus-restrictions (Arabian Business)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Russia]]
***[[Russia]] reports a record for the fourth consecutive day of 34,303 new cases of COVID-19, thereby bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 7.99 million. [https://www.euronews.com/2021/10/17/russia-reports-highest-daily-number-of-covid-19-cases (Euronews)]
*[[Japanese Prime Minister]] [[Fumio Kishida]] says that the mass release of wastewater at the [[Fukushima Daiichi Nuclear Power Plant|Fukushima nuclear plant]] cannot be delayed. The water, which has been inside the plant since the 2011 meltdown, is planned to be dumped into the [[Pacific Ocean]] over several decades despite strong opposition from local fishermen and the governments of [[China]] and [[South Korea]]. [https://www.channelnewsasia.com/asia/fumio-kishida-fukushima-wastewater-release-cannot-be-delayed-2250226 (CNA)]

'''International relations'''
*[[Foreign relations of Belarus]]
**The French ambassador to [[Belarus]] departs following a directive issued by the [[Government of Belarus|Belarusian government]], which did not cite a rationale. The ambassador had not presented his [[Letter of credence|credentials]] to [[President of Belarus|President]] [[Alexander Lukashenko]]. [https://www.themoscowtimes.com/2021/10/17/french-envoy-leaves-belarus-at-minsks-demand-embassy-a75320 (AFP via ''The Moscow Times'')]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[Honour killing in Pakistan]]
**A man is wanted in [[Pakistan]] after killing his two daughters and four grandchildren after [[Arson|setting their house ablaze]], as one of the daughters married against his wishes. Her husband also died in the fire. [https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/father-suspected-killing-daughters-grandchildren-pakistan-marriage-feud-police-2021-10-17/ (Reuters)]
*Authorities in [[Haiti]] says that members of the "[[400 Mawozo]]" gang are behind the [[kidnapping]] of 16 [[United States|American]] citizens and one [[Canada|Canadian]] citizen yesterday near [[Port-au-Prince]]. Those kidnapped include seven women, five men and five children. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-latin-america-58948107 (BBC News)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[2021 Cape Verdean presidential election]]
**Cape Verdeans head to the polls to elect their new president to replace outgoing term-limited president [[Jorge Carlos Fonseca]]. The candidates of Fonseca's [[right-wing]] [[Movement for Democracy (Cape Verde)|MpD]] and the leftist [[African Party for the Independence of Cape Verde|PAICV]] are the main contenders. The election is seen as important to reopen the important [[Tourism in Cape Verde|tourism industry]] which was hard-hit by the [[COVID-19 pandemic in Cape Verde|COVID-19 pandemic in the country]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/cape-verde-eyeing-economic-recovery-votes-new-president-2021-10-17/ (Reuters)]
*The [[Instituto Nacional Electoral]] in [[Mexico]] says that 2.85 million signatures are needed for a [[recall election]] against president [[Andrés Manuel López Obrador]]. Before becoming president, López Obrador had promised the referendum on himself to keep him accountable, although it is opposed by opposition parties, as they see it as a way to polarize voters and galvanize supporters of the president. [https://news.yahoo.com/mexican-electoral-body-says-2-170218925.html (''Yahoo! News'')]
